# Cowlendar

Cowlendar is a Shopify booking app operated by BOOKING APPOINTMENT COWLENDAR (SIREN 989 284 062), 14 rue Charles V, 75004 Paris, France.

## Product

Bookable Shopify services including appointments, group sessions, events, full-day and multi-day reservations. Integrations include Google Calendar, Outlook, Apple Calendar, Google Meet, Zoom, Microsoft Teams and Klaviyo; verify the exact setup with the documentation.

## Pricing checked September 22, 2026

- Free: 5 bookings/month, all features.
- Starter: $13.99/month, up to $1,000 booking revenue.
- Basic: $29.99/month, up to $3,000 booking revenue.
- Growth: $59.99/month, up to $10,000 booking revenue.

USD monthly prices. Verify current limits, taxes and usage charges on the official listing.

# 6 Best Shopify Appointment Booking Apps for Service Businesses (2026)

Compare the top 6 Shopify booking apps with real product images, feature-by-feature advice and monthly cost examples for appointments, classes and services.

- Canonical: https://cowlendar.com/blog/best-shopify-appointment-booking-apps-for-service-businesses-(2026)
- Published: 2026-06-26T00:00:00.000Z
- Updated: 2026-09-22T16:38:32.222451Z
- Publisher: Cowlendar

## The short answer

Our first pick is Cowlendar for a complete booking toolkit. Compare Meety, Apntly, Appointo, Easy Appointment Booking and BookX by the features you need and the plan you would actually pay for.

## The top 6, at a glance

**Our first pick is Cowlendar for service businesses that want appointments, classes, rentals and repeat bookings in one Shopify app.** Its free plan includes all features, so you can evaluate the workflow you actually want to launch. If your main need is a low fixed price for straightforward appointments, Apntly deserves a close look. For feature-based upgrades, Meety, Appointo, Easy Appointment Booking and BookX offer different paths.

This is a shortlist by the Cowlendar team. We make the first app on the list. The order reflects our editorial recommendations for service businesses, not an independent benchmark or an official Shopify ranking. Product facts come from official listings and documentation checked **September 22, 2026**. Images below are published by the respective app developers.

| Rank | App | Our pick for | Free offer | Relevant monthly paid price |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Cowlendar** | A complete booking toolkit across service types | All features; usage allowance applies | $13.99 Starter / $29.99 Basic / $59.99 Growth, by booking revenue |
| 2 | **Meety** | A broad feature ladder and customer workflows | Basic bookings and team members | $14 Starter for bundles; $47 Enterprise for deposits/API |
| 3 | **Apntly** | Low-cost appointment scheduling | One service and one team member | $9 Pro for calendar sync, groups and deposits |
| 4 | **Appointo** | Unlimited basic services with paid upgrades | Unlimited services and bookings | $14 Pro; add the listed 2% subscription/bundle charge when relevant |
| 5 | **Easy Appointment Booking** | Workshops, event operations and packs | One event or service | $39 Pro Plus for packs/deposits; $99 Ultimate for Klaviyo |
| 6 | **BookX** | Teams, locations and seasonal rental pricing | One service and one team member | $19.99 Growth for deposits; $39.99 Business for two-way Google sync |

Prices are USD on monthly billing, before taxes, Shopify/payment charges and optional add-ons. These are useful feature tiers, not equivalent packages. A free plan with all features is different from unlimited free booking volume. Cowlendar's [pricing page](/pricing) shows its usage allowances and revenue thresholds.

## 1. Cowlendar — best for a complete booking toolkit

<figure><img src="/assets/apps/cowlendar-screen.webp" alt="Cowlendar booking calendar and service interface from its official Shopify listing" width="1280" height="720" loading="lazy"><figcaption>Product image: <a href="https://apps.shopify.com/cowlendar">Cowlendar on the Shopify App Store</a>.</figcaption></figure>

<div class="ranked-facts"><p><strong>Best fit</strong>Appointments, classes, rentals and recurring services</p><p><strong>Starting point</strong>Free plan with all features</p><p><strong>Paid model</strong>Booking-revenue tiers</p><p><strong>Standout</strong>Bundles, subscriptions, equipment and automation</p></div>

A shop selling one-off consultations today may add a six-session coaching pack next month and a group workshop after that. Cowlendar is our recommendation when you want those offers to live in the same booking system. The feature set covers individual and group bookings, full-day and multi-day services, bundles, recurring subscriptions, deposits and prepayment.

The appeal is access to the real toolkit from the beginning. You can evaluate the booking format, calendar connection and payment workflow together instead of assembling a shortlist around several feature upgrades. The free plan includes all features; paid tiers increase the booking-revenue allowance.

### The advanced details worth knowing

- **Repeat visits:** offer booking bundles and recurring service subscriptions rather than treating every appointment as a separate sale.
- **Real availability:** work with service, teammate or equipment availability and participant categories.
- **Connected operations:** the beta public API can read services and bookings, create a manual booking and attach it to a subscription credit.
- **Useful events:** beta webhooks include attendance changes and failed subscription billing, alongside booking lifecycle events. Signed payloads and delivery retries are documented.

**What would you pay?** At 20 bookings × $40, monthly booking revenue is $800: Starter is $13.99. At $2,000, Basic is $29.99. At $4,000, Growth is $59.99. The listed ceilings are $1,000, $3,000 and $10,000 respectively. Optional messaging charges and other applicable costs remain separate.

**Check before choosing:** the API is beta. API-created bookings do not create a Shopify order, and the current API does not offer available-slot lookup or booking update/delete endpoints. Use the [API and webhook documentation](https://help.cowlendar.com/how-to-integrations/connect-cowlendar-to-crm-erp-or-app-public-api-webhooks) to validate a custom integration.

<div class="ranking-callout"><p><strong>Our verdict:</strong> the strongest starting point on this shortlist for a merchant who wants several booking formats, advanced functions and room to evolve the offer. Also: a cow named after a calendar is a pretty good conversation starter.</p></div>

## 2. Meety — best for a broad feature ladder

<figure><img src="/assets/apps/meety-screen.webp" alt="Meety appointment booking calendar shown on its official Shopify listing" width="1280" height="720" loading="lazy"><figcaption>Product image: <a href="https://apps.shopify.com/meety-appointment-booking">Meety on Shopify</a>.</figcaption></figure>

<div class="ranked-facts"><p><strong>Best fit</strong>Teams choosing features one tier at a time</p><p><strong>Relevant price</strong>$14 Starter / $27 Business / $47 Enterprise</p></div>

Meety is worth considering when you like its customer journey and want to add capabilities through progressively higher tiers. It is a real contender for repeat-booking businesses: subscriptions and bundles are documented, and its official help center also describes webhook integrations.

The pricing distinction matters. Starter includes bundles, subscriptions, Google Calendar and Zoom. Business adds Outlook, waitlists and the team portal. The listing places deposits, Klaviyo, Zapier and API integration on Enterprise.

**What would you pay?** A merchant needing bundles and deposits should budget $47/month from the listed Enterprise upgrade, rather than the $7 entry plan. For the same requested features at $800 booking revenue, Cowlendar Starter is $13.99. At $4,000 revenue, Cowlendar Growth is $59.99, so Meety's fixed plan becomes less expensive in that scenario.

**Check before choosing:** Meety's webhook documentation uses the plan name “Premium,” while its listing uses a different tier structure. Confirm the current webhook entitlement and messaging charges directly.

## How to choose the right Shopify booking app

**Write the workflow before choosing the plan.** List the services, staff, equipment, booking formats and payment rules you need. Specify whether a calendar connection must import busy time, export appointments or do both. Decide whether recurring customers buy separate sessions, a prepaid pack or a renewing subscription.

**Price a normal month and a busy month.** The [comparison directory](/compare) includes calculators for ten apps, with booking volume, average value and feature requirements. Keep app subscriptions separate from Shopify costs, payment processing, messaging and extra staff access. Use the [service price calculator](/free-tools/service-price-calculator) to check your own service economics.

**Test the awkward booking.** Fill the last seat, create an external calendar conflict, move an appointment and cancel a paid reservation. Confirm which emails fire and how the booking, order and refund records change. For an API integration, inspect the actual endpoints and event payloads.

**Make the schedule realistic.** Use our [time slot generator](/free-tools/time-slot-generator) to plan service duration and buffer time. Use the [no-show calculator](/free-tools/no-show-calculator) to put numbers on missed visits, without assuming that any app guarantees a particular improvement.

## What about rental specialists and larger retail teams?

This top six focuses on general service businesses. **IzyRent** is another useful option for rental-first stores, especially when date-based rates and iCalendar connections matter. **BookThatApp** is worth considering for specialized resource and bond workflows. **Sesami** belongs on an agency-led retail shortlist when an SDK is part of the brief.

Explore [Cowlendar vs IzyRent](/cowlendar-vs-izyrent), [Cowlendar vs BookThatApp](/cowlendar-vs-book-that-app) and [Cowlendar vs Sesami](/cowlendar-vs-sesami) for their separate tradeoffs. The best selection is the app whose documented behavior matches the business you want to run.

Advanced capabilities are checked against the vendor's documentation where available. We distinguish a confirmed limitation from a capability that was not established in those sources.

## Common questions

### What is the best Shopify booking app for service businesses?

Our first pick is Cowlendar when you need appointments, group sessions, rentals, bundles and subscriptions in one app. Apntly is a useful low-cost appointment option; Meety, Appointo, Easy Appointment Booking and BookX offer other feature and pricing tradeoffs. This is an editorial recommendation by the Cowlendar team.

### Does Cowlendar have a free plan with all features?

Yes. Cowlendar’s free plan includes all features. Usage allowances apply; consult the pricing page for the free allowance, revenue thresholds and optional charges.

### Can Shopify sell appointments without a booking app?

Shopify supports service products, but appointment availability and scheduling normally require a booking app or a custom integration.

### Which Shopify booking apps support subscriptions or bundles?

Cowlendar, Meety and Appointo list subscriptions and bundles. Easy Appointment Booking lists booking packs, while BookX lists bundle bookings. Confirm the applicable tier and any transaction-linked charge.

### Is the cheapest starting price the best comparison?

No. Compare the required plan for your calendars, deposits, bundles, staff access and integrations. Include usage charges and test both a typical and a busy month.

# Five Practical Ways to Reduce No-Shows for Shopify Bookings

Improve attendance with clear confirmations, useful reminders, easy rescheduling, appropriate payment terms and a measurable follow-up process.

- Canonical: https://cowlendar.com/blog/5-powerful-strategies-to-instantly-reduce-no-shows-and-boost-sales-in-your-shopify-store
- Published: 2025-07-01T00:00:00.000Z
- Updated: 2026-09-22T10:00:00Z
- Publisher: Cowlendar

## The short answer

Reduce preventable confusion and make changes easy before increasing penalties. Measure attendance and late cancellations separately; no tactic guarantees a specific improvement.

## 1. Make the confirmation impossible to misunderstand
Show the booked service, date, local time, time zone, location or meeting link, and the customer's next action. Use an explicit date rather than an ambiguous numeric format when serving international customers.

Test the confirmation on a phone and in a different time zone. If customers cannot quickly find where to go or how to join, another reminder will repeat the same problem rather than solve it.

## 2. Send reminders that let people act
A useful reminder includes a clear way to confirm, reschedule within policy or contact the business. Choose timing that gives customers a realistic opportunity to respond and gives you time to refill the slot.

Do not assume more messages are always better. Review delivery failures, customer feedback and actual attendance. SMS and other channels can carry usage costs and consent requirements, so configure them for your audience and applicable rules.

## 3. Make permitted changes easier than disappearing
If a customer knows they cannot attend, a simple rescheduling path can preserve the relationship and release the original time. State the cutoff clearly and show the next available options.

Test the change flow from the customer's confirmation email. Verify the old slot is released, the new slot is reserved, and both staff and customer receive the updated details. Keep cancellations, reschedules and no-shows as separate statuses in reporting.

## 4. Use payment terms that fit the service
Full prepayment or a booking advance may be appropriate where missed appointments create preparation costs. That does not mean deposits always improve conversion or attendance. Make the terms clear before booking and evaluate the effect for your business.

Check the refund and remaining-balance process with the actual payment setup. A payment policy should be understandable and workable, not merely a deterrent copied from another company.

## 5. Learn from missed appointments
Use a short, respectful follow-up to understand whether the problem was timing, unclear instructions, a technical issue or something else. Do not expose private information or pressure the customer into sharing unnecessary details.

| Metric | What it helps distinguish |
| --- | --- |
| Attended bookings / expected bookings | Actual attendance outcome |
| Cancellations before cutoff | Timely changes that may release capacity |
| Late cancellations | Lost preparation or refill time |
| Reschedules completed | Demand retained at another time |
| Failed reminder deliveries | Contact or notification problems |

Compare similar services and periods. A change in service mix or advertising audience can affect the numbers, so avoid attributing every improvement to the latest reminder template.

## Put the workflow into your booking system
Cowlendar lists reminders, cancellation/rescheduling and payment options. Configure these together around a clear policy, then test the full customer journey. Our [cancellation guide](/blog/manage-cancellations-and-rescheduling-in-shopify-bookings) covers the operational details.

Start with the most common preventable problem. If people arrive at the wrong location, fix the address and directions. If they forget, test useful reminders. If they cannot change a booking, improve that path. Specific fixes are more credible than a promised percentage reduction.

## Official sources
- [Cowlendar reminders and booking management](https://apps.shopify.com/cowlendar)
- [Shopify refund handling](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/orders/refund-cancel-order)


## Common questions

### How much will reminders reduce no-shows?

There is no guaranteed percentage for your business. Measure comparable bookings before and after the change, including delivery failures and cancellations.

### Are deposits always the best solution?

No. First identify why customers miss appointments. Payment terms may help some services, while clearer instructions or easier rescheduling may address other causes.

# Hotel Booking on Shopify: Rooms, Nights & Daily Operations

Plan hotel bookings on Shopify with a room inventory checklist, arrival and departure rules, payment checks and a practical launch test.

- Canonical: https://cowlendar.com/blog/best-booking-apps-for-hotels-on-shopify
- Published: 2025-07-30T00:00:00.000Z
- Updated: 2026-09-22T10:00:00Z
- Publisher: Cowlendar

## The short answer

For hotels, the hardest question is not how the calendar looks. It is whether every occupied night and every room are accounted for correctly.

## Map rooms before mapping screens
List each room or room category and its sellable quantity. Include rooms temporarily unavailable for maintenance and any rooms you reserve for direct requests. Decide whether staff assign an exact room after booking or whether the customer chooses it upfront.

For a small property, a Shopify booking app can support a direct-sales workflow. For a larger hotel, front-desk operations, housekeeping, channel distribution and reporting may require a dedicated property-management system. Do not remove those systems simply because a booking app displays a date picker.

## Check arrival and departure logic
A guest checking in on June 10 and leaving on June 12 normally occupies two nights. Test how the app counts that interval, and whether another guest may arrive on the 12th. Add the appropriate cleaning or turnaround window where the product supports it.

Try a stay that crosses a month boundary, a daylight-saving change and a blocked maintenance date. These edge cases reveal problems that a simple one-night test will miss. Use the property's local timezone consistently in staff views and confirmation messages.

## Compare the relevant booking models
Cowlendar and BookX explicitly list multi-day booking, while BookThatApp describes rental and hotel scheduling. These are candidates for a direct-booking implementation. Their public descriptions do not establish every PMS or channel-management requirement.

| Operational question | Evidence to request |
| --- | --- |
| Can the last room be sold only once? | Two simultaneous booking attempts |
| Can an existing stay change dates? | Availability before and after the change |
| Does each channel share inventory? | A demonstrated connection and refresh behavior |
| Can staff block maintenance? | A block that affects every sales path |
| Are extras priced correctly? | A complete test checkout with all fees |

Our [hotel app comparison guide](/blog/best-shopify-hotel-and-vacation-rental-booking-apps-in-2026) helps build the shortlist. Use the [multi-day setup guide](/blog/how-to-manage-multi-day-rental-bookings-on-shopify) for interval testing.

## Build a daily front-desk routine
Give the team a consistent arrival list, departure list and unresolved-payment list. Include only the information they need for the task. Confirm who can alter reservations and how changes are communicated to the guest and cleaning team.

A booking record, a Shopify order and a payment transaction are related but not identical. If a stay is cancelled, verify the inventory change and the financial action separately. Do not assume a calendar cancellation automatically returns money.

## Explain the stay before payment
Show arrival hours, departure time, occupancy, accessibility information, location and cancellation terms on the product page. Clarify whether the initial amount is a full payment, an advance toward the stay or a separate refundable deposit.

Avoid burying essential restrictions in a reminder sent after checkout. Customers should understand the practical conditions before committing, and the confirmation should repeat the most useful arrival details.

## Reconcile before opening the calendar
Export or list every future stay, including offline reservations and room blocks. Check the new calendar against that list date by date. Make a small controlled booking and refund test, then open a limited date range first.

Keep the previous reservation records accessible during the transition. If an integration cannot demonstrate reliable cross-channel inventory behavior, use a request-to-book process or keep the established channel manager until the issue is resolved.

## Official sources
- [Cowlendar rental and multi-day features](https://apps.shopify.com/cowlendar)
- [BookX multi-day booking](https://apps.shopify.com/appointment-booking-bookeasy)
- [BookThatApp booking types](https://apps.shopify.com/bookthatapp)


## Common questions

### Can I sell room nights as a normal Shopify product?

A normal product quantity does not by itself reserve availability across a date range. Use and test a booking workflow that models each occupied night and room capacity.

### Should I cancel my hotel management software?

Only after verifying every operational requirement. A Shopify booking app is not automatically a replacement for a PMS, housekeeping system or channel manager.

# How to Choose a Nail Salon Booking App for Shopify in 2026

Evaluate nail salon booking on Shopify with treatment durations, technician skills, add-ons, cleanup time and repeat-customer workflows.

- Canonical: https://cowlendar.com/blog/best-nail-salon-booking-app-for-shopify-in-2026
- Published: 2026-07-05T00:00:00.000Z
- Updated: 2026-09-22T16:38:32.222451Z
- Publisher: Cowlendar

## The short answer

Choose a booking app that reflects the time and technician each treatment actually needs. Removal, repair and nail-art add-ons must not silently overrun the next appointment.

## Build a menu around duration, not just names
A manicure, gel removal and a detailed nail-art appointment can take very different amounts of time. Define each service clearly and explain what is included. If an add-on changes the duration, the booking setup needs to reserve that extra time.

Avoid accepting a short basic appointment while asking customers to describe unlimited extras in a notes field. Use defined options or a consultation route for work that requires an assessment.

## Match treatments to qualified technicians
A customer choosing “any technician” should only see staff who can perform the selected treatment. Give each person a realistic schedule, breaks and preparation time. Where equipment or stations are shared, protect that resource as well.

| Booking detail | Test before launch |
| --- | --- |
| Removal before a new set | Duration expands as intended |
| Detailed nail art | Suitable technician and sufficient time |
| Two customers booking together | Correct number of staff and stations |
| Repair appointment | Clear scope and appropriately short slot |
| Cleanup buffer | The next customer cannot book inside it |

## Compare apps by workflow and plan
For a solo technician with a simple offer, Apntly and Appointo have free entry points worth evaluating. Cowlendar provides its feature set on the free plan, with paid booking-revenue tiers. Tipo offers staff and service limits by plan.

These are starting points, not a guarantee that every add-on or paired appointment works identically. Show the vendor a realistic service combination and ask them to demonstrate it on the plan you would use.

## Make repeat visits easy without creating confusion
If you sell a treatment pack, distinguish purchasing the pack from reserving each visit. Check how credits are redeemed, what happens after a cancellation and whether customers can see their remaining entitlement.

For recurring appointments, verify how changes to one visit affect the series. A customer moving a single appointment should not unintentionally move every future reservation.

## Set clear payment and cancellation expectations
Show the amount due now, any remaining balance and the applicable change deadline. If a deposit is required, describe its purpose accurately. Check refunds and booking cancellations separately.

Reminders should include the service, date, location and a useful change link. Preparation instructions should be relevant and concise. Avoid filling messages with marketing content that makes the appointment details harder to find.

## Run a realistic half-day trial
Create several consecutive appointments with different durations. Add a staff break, a late change and a treatment requiring a specific technician. Ask the team whether the resulting schedule is workable.

The best app is the one that passes this practical test and remains affordable at your expected volume. Use our [salon app comparison](/blog/best-shopify-booking-apps-for-salons-and-spas-in-2026-reviews-and-pricing) for a wider shortlist.

## Official sources
- [Cowlendar](https://apps.shopify.com/cowlendar)
- [Apntly](https://apps.shopify.com/appointly)
- [Appointo](https://apps.shopify.com/appointo-appointments-and-bookings)
- [Tipo](https://apps.shopify.com/tipo-appointment-booking)


## Common questions

### Can nail-art add-ons extend appointment duration?

That depends on the app and configuration. Verify that the selected option changes occupied time, not just the price.

### Should I offer an “any technician” option?

It can simplify booking if the system only includes qualified, available staff and protects the required station or equipment.

# Best Shopify Rental Apps: Equipment, Dates & Deposits (2026)

Compare Shopify rental booking apps for equipment, date ranges, stock and deposits. Learn what to test before you start taking reservations.

- Canonical: https://cowlendar.com/blog/best-shopify-apps-for-rental-businesses-in-2026
- Published: 2026-06-23T00:00:00.000Z
- Updated: 2026-09-22T10:00:00Z
- Publisher: Cowlendar

## The short answer

Choose a rental app by how it reserves resources over time. Selling a product quantity is not enough to guarantee that equipment is available for the entire rental.

## Define what one rental consumes
List the resources required by a booking: the item, accessories, staff time and any preparation or cleaning period. A kayak booking might consume a boat, paddle and guide. A camera rental may reserve a particular kit for several consecutive days. The reservation must protect the scarce resource for the whole interval.

Write down your inventory units before installing an app. Decide whether customers select a named item or any available unit within a category. That distinction affects how you handle substitutions, repairs and maintenance.

## Which apps belong on the shortlist?
Cowlendar, BookX and BookThatApp advertise rental-oriented or multi-day capabilities. Tipo also lists full-day and multi-day booking on Basic. These are candidates to test against your inventory model, not interchangeable rental-management systems.

| Situation | Candidates to investigate | Important test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rentals alongside appointments and classes | Cowlendar, BookX | One resource shared between service types |
| Equipment with deposits or bonds | BookThatApp, Cowlendar | Distinguish a booking payment from a damage bond |
| Seasonal rental prices | BookX | A date range crossing two price periods |
| A small catalogue and staff team | Tipo | Resource count and overlapping intervals |

The [comparison library](/compare) links to each vendor's official listing and shows plan limits. Use current quotes for any special inventory or payment requirement.

## Test overlapping dates, not only identical start times
Create a reservation from Monday morning to Wednesday evening. A second reservation starting Tuesday must not be accepted for the same unit just because its start time differs. Then try a reservation after the configured turnaround buffer; it should become available when the equipment is genuinely ready.

Test cancellations and early returns too. The inventory should recover according to your intended process. If an app requires a manual action to reopen stock, make that task explicit for the team.

## Deposits need a clear definition
An advance payment contributes to the rental price. A refundable damage deposit protects against a different risk. A card authorization is different again: it has processor-specific rules and is not the same as taking a payment and refunding it later.

Ask the app and payment provider to demonstrate the exact mechanism you need. Show the customer what is charged now, what remains due, when a refundable amount is returned, and how a dispute is handled. Our [rental deposit workflow](/blog/how-to-build-a-rental-damage-deposit-workflow-that-protects-you) separates these steps.

## Make pickup and return usable
Tell customers where to collect the item, what to bring and how late returns affect their booking. Include opening hours and the correct timezone. If the return location differs from pickup, collect that choice before payment and check that your operations can support it.

Use custom questions for useful logistics, not as a substitute for inventory rules. Asking “which bike do you want?” does not reserve that bike unless the answer is connected to an actual resource allocation.

## Compare the total cost
Model a quiet month and a busy month. Count bookings, revenue, team accounts, locations and integrations. Cowlendar's published tiers scale with booking revenue; BookThatApp lists booking-volume limits; BookX and Tipo use their own feature and team/service tiers. The cheapest entry plan may not cover peak season.

Before switching, import or manually reconcile every future reservation and blackout period. Keep a dated inventory snapshot, then test one real item from booking to return. Avoid running two independently bookable calendars against the same stock.

## Official sources
- [Cowlendar](https://apps.shopify.com/cowlendar)
- [BookX](https://apps.shopify.com/appointment-booking-bookeasy)
- [BookThatApp](https://apps.shopify.com/bookthatapp)
- [Tipo Appointment Booking](https://apps.shopify.com/tipo-appointment-booking)


## Common questions

### Can I rent physical products on Shopify?

Yes, with a workflow that handles date-based availability and rental operations. Verify resource allocation, overlapping dates, pickup, returns and payments before launch.

### Is a rental deposit the same as a booking deposit?

No. A booking deposit is usually an advance toward the price. A refundable damage deposit or card authorization has a different purpose and needs its own clearly documented process.

# Best Shopify Booking Apps for Yoga & Fitness Classes (2026)

Compare yoga and fitness booking apps for Shopify by class capacity, passes, waitlists, instructor schedules and real operating costs.

- Canonical: https://cowlendar.com/blog/best-shopify-booking-app-for-yoga-studios-and-fitness-classes-(2026)
- Published: 2026-07-22T00:00:00.000Z
- Updated: 2026-09-22T16:38:32.222451Z
- Publisher: Cowlendar

## The short answer

A class booking needs both a seat and an available instructor or room. Test those constraints together before choosing an app for your studio.

## Decide whether you sell a seat, a pass or a membership
A single drop-in class reserves one seat in one session. A five-class pass creates a balance that the customer redeems over time. A membership may involve recurring billing and rules about what can be booked. Those are separate workflows; support for one does not prove support for the others.

Write down your actual policy: how many sessions a pass includes, when credits expire, whether a cancellation restores a credit, and whether no-shows consume one. Then ask the vendor to demonstrate that policy rather than accepting the word “subscription” as a complete answer.

## Compare apps by the class operation
Cowlendar lists group bookings, bundles and subscriptions. Easy Appointment Booking lists booking packs and waitlists on Pro Plus. Meety documents bundles/subscriptions on Starter and waitlists on Business. Sesami lists group appointments on Pro. These are useful starting points, with different plan structures and prices.

| Studio requirement | What to verify |
| --- | --- |
| Drop-in classes | Per-session capacity and a clear attendee count |
| Shared studio room | Two instructors cannot reserve the room simultaneously |
| Passes | Purchase, redemption, remaining balance and expiry |
| Waitlist | How a released place is offered and how long it is held |
| Recurring payments | Billing, failed payments, cancellation and booking entitlement |
| Instructor changes | Substitute coverage without duplicating the class |

See [Cowlendar vs Easy Appointment Booking](/cowlendar-vs-easy-appointment-booking) and [Cowlendar vs Meety](/cowlendar-vs-meety) for sourced feature and pricing comparisons.

## Check what happens when a class fills up
Create a class with a capacity of three, then reserve three seats across different customers. Try adding a fourth. Next cancel one reservation and confirm the capacity and any waitlist update as expected.

Test multi-seat bookings separately. If a customer brings two friends, the booking should consume three places, not one. Decide whether you need each attendee's name or only the purchaser's contact information.

## Make the timetable easy to understand
Use consistent class names, difficulty levels, durations and locations. Describe equipment provided, arrival time and any access instructions. A class description should let a newcomer decide whether the session is suitable without needing a support conversation.

On mobile, the customer should be able to see the date, start time, instructor and price without jumping between several pages. If you offer online classes, display the timezone and send the meeting link through the intended confirmation workflow.

## Budget for the studio you are becoming
Calculate the next six months of expected bookings and revenue, then include staff logins, required integrations and any messaging or subscription charges. Some free plans are generous for a single service; they may still lack the pass or calendar behavior you need.

Cowlendar's free plan with all features is a small test allowance. A studio running daily classes should compare the relevant paid revenue tier with the competitor plan that actually includes groups, passes and waitlists.

## Pilot one recurring class
Start with one class type and two weeks of dates. Test payment, cancellation, a full class, a substitute instructor and a credit redemption if you sell packs. Keep your current attendance records until the new system's counts are reconciled.

If you are already committed to Shopify and need setup guidance, follow [yoga and wellness booking setup](/blog/how-to-offer-yoga-and-wellness-class-bookings-on-shopify). A separate studio-management platform may still be needed for requirements outside booking and commerce.

## Official sources
- [Cowlendar plans and formats](https://apps.shopify.com/cowlendar)
- [Easy Appointment Booking packs and waitlists](https://apps.shopify.com/appointments-and-bookings)
- [Meety feature tiers](https://apps.shopify.com/meety-appointment-booking)
- [Sesami group appointments](https://apps.shopify.com/sesami)


## Common questions

### Can a Shopify booking app manage a class pass?

Some apps document bundles or packs. Verify credit balances, expiry, cancellation restoration and the exact plan before selling your pass.

### Is a subscription the same as class access?

No. Recurring payment and permission to reserve classes are separate behaviors that must be connected and tested.

# Best Shopify Booking Apps for Salons and Spas in 2026

Compare salon and spa booking apps for Shopify by staff, treatment rooms, reminders, deposits and the cost of the required plan.

- Canonical: https://cowlendar.com/blog/best-shopify-booking-apps-for-salons-and-spas-in-2026-reviews-and-pricing
- Published: 2026-06-27T00:00:00.000Z
- Updated: 2026-09-22T16:38:32.222451Z
- Publisher: Cowlendar

## The short answer

Choose around the treatment workflow: qualified staff, required space, realistic duration and customer changes. A salon needs dependable availability more than a long feature list.

## Start with your hardest treatment to schedule
A simple haircut can be easier to model than a treatment requiring a specialist, a room and preparation time. Evaluate apps against the most important constraint first. If the system cannot protect that resource combination, an attractive booking page will not solve the operational problem.

This shortlist reflects documented product capabilities, not hands-on testing of every salon configuration. Verify plan details and demonstrate your own workflow before committing.

| Salon situation | Apps to investigate | What to test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Solo practitioner, one service | Apntly, Appointo | Free-plan limits and calendar conflicts |
| Several treatment types | Cowlendar, Meety | Staff skills, rooms and customer changes |
| Retail store adding consultations | Sesami, Cowlendar | POS workflow and staff/resource model |
| Repeat visits and packages | Easy Appointment Booking, Appointo | Credit redemption, expiry and extra charges |
| Team with clear service limits | Tipo, BookX | Required tier as staff and locations grow |

## Compare the complete monthly cost
Apntly lists paid plans from $5 and a $9 Pro plan with groups, calendar integrations and deposits. Cowlendar starts at $13.99 after its free plan, with tiers tied to booking revenue. Tipo lists Basic at $9.90 and Pro at $14.90 with different staff and service limits.

These are monthly USD figures checked September 22, 2026. They do not imply that the entry tier of every app includes the same workflow. Add applicable staff, messaging, package or payment costs to the comparison.

## Verify staff and room availability together
Book the same therapist into two services that use different rooms. Then book two therapists into the same room. The setup should block whichever shared resource is unavailable.

Test buffers around treatments and the handling of staff breaks. If customers can choose “any available professional,” verify the system only assigns people qualified for that treatment.

## Look beyond the first appointment
A useful salon workflow handles rescheduling, late cancellations, repeat visits and package use. Make a booking, change it and check both the calendar and payment status. If customers buy a course of treatments, confirm how individual visits are reserved and consumed.

Ask whether the app replaces any existing salon tools or merely adds online booking. Inventory, commissions, clinical records and payroll are separate requirements unless explicitly supported.

## Make the team part of the trial
A receptionist should be able to find a customer's appointment, understand the service and payment status, and make an allowed change. A practitioner should see the information needed for the day without unnecessary access to unrelated customer data.

Choose the app that passes those operational tests on a sustainable plan. For step-by-step setup, use our [salon and spa implementation guide](/blog/how-to-set-up-salon-and-spa-appointments-on-shopify).

# Shopify Hotel & Vacation Rental Booking Apps: What to Compare (2026)

Choose a Shopify hotel or vacation rental booking app with a practical checklist for nights, availability, payments and channel synchronization.

- Canonical: https://cowlendar.com/blog/best-shopify-hotel-and-vacation-rental-booking-apps-in-2026
- Published: 2026-06-28T00:00:00.000Z
- Updated: 2026-09-22T10:00:00Z
- Publisher: Cowlendar

## The short answer

A Shopify booking app can support direct stays, but it is not automatically a hotel property-management system or an Airbnb channel manager.

## Start with the property model
A single vacation cottage, six identical rooms and a hotel with several room categories are three different inventory problems. Before comparing apps, write down exactly what can be reserved and what should become unavailable after a booking.

For a cottage, one reservation usually blocks the whole property for a date range. For identical rooms, you need a capacity count for each overlapping night. For a hotel with named rooms, you may need room assignment as well as category availability. Test the most complicated version you actually sell.

## Build a shortlist around your requirements
Cowlendar, BookX and BookThatApp document rental or multi-day booking workflows. That makes them reasonable Shopify candidates to investigate, not proof that each meets every hospitality requirement. Our detailed [BookX comparison](/cowlendar-vs-bookx) and [BookThatApp comparison](/cowlendar-vs-book-that-app) explain the relevant plan distinctions.

| Requirement | What a successful test looks like |
| --- | --- |
| Night-based availability | A Tuesday check-in and Friday check-out occupies three nights |
| Same-day turnover | A departing guest does not incorrectly block the next permitted arrival |
| Minimum stay | A one-night selection is refused when your rule requires two |
| Room capacity | The last available unit disappears after a confirmed reservation |
| Fees | Cleaning, extras and taxes appear clearly before payment |
| Changes | Shortening or cancelling a stay updates availability correctly |

## Be precise about calendar connections
Google Calendar synchronization is not the same as synchronizing availability with Airbnb, Booking.com or a property-management system. Likewise, an iCalendar export may be a periodically refreshed feed rather than a real-time conflict check. Ask each vendor which direction data moves, how often it refreshes, and what happens when two channels receive a booking close together.

If multiple channels sell the same property, choose a verified source of truth for inventory. Do not activate instant booking on a new channel until you have demonstrated the overlap protection. Where a dedicated channel manager is necessary, treat the Shopify app as one part of the stack.

## Price a realistic stay
Use one short stay, one longer stay and one stay crossing a seasonal price boundary. Check whether pricing is per night, per day, per guest or a fixed booking amount. Confirm how extras and discounts interact with that calculation.

Cowlendar's current published plans use booking-revenue tiers. BookX lists seasonal-pricing capabilities on paid tiers. BookThatApp's public plans use booking-volume and staff limits. Compare the applicable plan using expected turnover and booking volume, not just the number of properties.

## Set expectations before checkout
The product page should explain check-in and check-out times, maximum occupancy, location, included amenities and the cancellation policy. A booking payment or advance payment is not necessarily a refundable damage bond; describe each amount separately.

Collect only the information needed at reservation time. Put operational arrival instructions in the confirmation message and send sensitive access details through an appropriate process. Never put door codes in a publicly accessible calendar description.

## A safe launch sequence
Start with one property or room category. Make a test reservation, change its dates, cancel it, and repeat the process on mobile. Verify the order amount, confirmation email and blocked nights each time. Reconcile existing stays before opening dates to the public.

If you need an implementation walkthrough rather than an app shortlist, follow our [Airbnb-style booking guide](/blog/how-to-offer-airbnb-style-bookings-on-your-shopify-store). For room operations, see [hotel booking on Shopify](/blog/best-booking-apps-for-hotels-on-shopify).

## Official sources
- [Cowlendar booking formats and pricing](https://apps.shopify.com/cowlendar)
- [BookX multi-day and seasonal options](https://apps.shopify.com/appointment-booking-bookeasy)
- [BookThatApp rental scheduling](https://apps.shopify.com/bookthatapp)


## Common questions

### Can Shopify replace my hotel PMS?

A store and booking app may cover direct reservations, but you should separately verify room assignment, housekeeping, channel management and reporting requirements.

### Does Google Calendar sync prevent double bookings across Airbnb and Booking.com?

Not by itself. Verify a specific channel integration or inventory synchronization workflow with the vendors involved.

# Best Website Builders for Online Booking: Shopify, Wix, Squarespace and WordPress

Compare booking website approaches by commerce needs, maintenance, scheduling tools and total cost—not just the design template.

- Canonical: https://cowlendar.com/blog/best-website-builders-for-online-booking-systems
- Published: 2026-07-02T00:00:00.000Z
- Updated: 2026-09-22T10:00:00Z
- Publisher: Cowlendar

## The short answer

Choose the website platform around the business you run. Shopify suits commerce-led services, while a simpler appointment site or a highly customized system may fit a different platform.

## Start with the role of the website
A booking website can be a simple appointment page, a product-and-service store, a class schedule or a rental catalog. Before choosing a builder, identify what customers must buy and what your team must manage afterward.

This is a workflow comparison, not a claim that one platform is best for every business. Plan inclusions and prices change, so verify the linked official documentation before purchasing.

| Platform approach | Worth considering when | Main thing to evaluate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shopify with a booking app | Products and services should share a commerce storefront | App workflow, Shopify costs and order integration |
| Wix with Wix Bookings | The website and service scheduling are the main project | Required site plan, service types and payment setup |
| Squarespace with Acuity | A design-led site needs a dedicated scheduling experience | Acuity subscription and how it connects to the site |
| WordPress with WooCommerce Bookings | You want control and can maintain the system | Hosting, extensions, updates and resource configuration |

## Shopify: useful when booking belongs in commerce
Shopify supports selling services, with a suitable booking app adding scheduling. This can make sense when customers browse physical products and appointments in the same store, or when your team already works with Shopify orders.

Evaluate the combined cost of Shopify, the booking app and payment processing. Cowlendar is one option, but our [comparison directory](/compare) covers several alternatives. The right app must handle your duration, capacity and payment requirements.

## Wix: evaluate the booking-enabled site plan
Wix Bookings supports service scheduling within a Wix site. Its documentation says you can add the app for free, but the site must be upgraded to accept bookings. Check the exact plan and payment capabilities for your region and business.

Test the service types you need—such as appointments, classes or courses—and how staff availability works. A builder's attractive templates do not prove it can enforce every resource conflict.

## Squarespace and Acuity: understand the separate system
Squarespace scheduling blocks can display an Acuity scheduler. An Acuity subscription is part of the setup; do not assume the website subscription alone includes the scheduling service you need.

Evaluate booking questions, calendars, reminders and payment behavior in Acuity, then test how customers move between the website and scheduler. Keep product purchases and appointment records conceptually distinct unless your configuration explicitly connects them.

## WordPress and WooCommerce: more ownership, more upkeep
WooCommerce Bookings provides a bookable-product model, with documented concepts such as persons and resources. It is worth investigating when you need control and have the skills or support to maintain a WordPress stack.

Include hosting, backups, security updates, extension compatibility and development work in the budget. A flexible system still needs someone responsible when a theme update changes the booking page.

## Compare a complete customer journey
Build or view a representative service on each shortlisted platform. Check mobile booking, payment, confirmation, cancellation and staff access. For rentals or shared resources, attempt an overlapping reservation.

Then ask who will maintain the system six months from now. The best choice balances the customer experience with the team's ability to operate it reliably. If you already have a working Shopify store, changing the entire platform may create more work than selecting the right booking app.

## Official sources
- [Shopify: selling services](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/digital-service-product/selling-services-or-digital-products)
- [Wix: about Wix Bookings](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-bookings-about-wix-bookings)
- [Squarespace: scheduling blocks](https://support.squarespace.com/hc/en-us/articles/206545577-Scheduling-blocks)
- [WooCommerce Bookings documentation](https://woocommerce.com/documentation/products/extensions/woocommerce-bookings/)


## Common questions

### Do all website builders include booking for free?

No. Scheduling may require a paid website plan, a separate subscription or a paid extension. Compare the complete setup.

### Should I move away from Shopify to add appointments?

Not necessarily. If the store already fits your commerce needs, test suitable Shopify booking apps before taking on a platform migration.

# Cowlendar vs Appointo in 2026: Free Limits, Paid Features and Booking Fit

Compare Cowlendar and Appointo for Shopify, including free booking allowances, calendar sync, packages and paid-plan costs.

- Published: 2026-06-19T00:00:00.000Z
- Updated: 2026-09-22T16:38:32.222451Z
- Publisher: Cowlendar

## The short answer

Appointo is worth considering for unlimited free bookings with feature-based upgrades. Cowlendar offers a small free allowance and a common feature set across booking-revenue tiers.

## The main difference is the upgrade path
Both apps address Shopify booking needs, but the pricing models ask different questions. With Cowlendar, estimate booking volume during the free allowance and booking revenue on paid tiers. With Appointo, identify the plan containing your required features and any applicable usage charges.

Our [permanent Cowlendar vs Appointo page](/cowlendar-vs-appointo) contains the detailed feature table. This guide focuses on how to evaluate the choice for your store. It is written by the Cowlendar team, not an independent testing organization.

## Compare the free plans honestly
Appointo's listing includes unlimited services and bookings on the free plan, plus multi-day booking. Calendar integrations and reminders are listed on paid plans. Cowlendar's free plan includes all features on the free plan.

If your ongoing needs fit Appointo's free capabilities, that is a meaningful advantage. If you need to evaluate several advanced booking features with a few test reservations, Cowlendar's allowance may be useful. Neither conclusion requires pretending the two free offers are identical.

| Decision | Cowlendar | Appointo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free booking volume | 5/month | Unlimited listed |
| Paid structure | Booking-revenue tiers | Feature tiers |
| Entry paid price | $13.99/month | $14/month |
| Groups | Included feature set | Premium listed at $25/month |
| Advanced portals/add-ons | Verify the precise workflow | Advanced listed at $39/month |
| Subscription/bundle charges | Confirm any applicable usage costs | 2% charge disclosed in paid-plan descriptions |

Prices are monthly USD checked September 22, 2026; Shopify, taxes and applicable usage costs are separate.

## Test the features that define your business
For appointments, test external calendar conflicts and customer rescheduling. For groups, test participant capacity and changing one attendee in a multi-person booking. For rentals, test overlapping dates and the end-date boundary.

If you sell repeat-visit packages, follow the complete path from purchase to redeemed sessions. Check expiration, cancellation and reporting, and include any percentage-based charges in the business model.

## Evaluate customer and team access
A portal can be valuable when customers or staff need regular access to bookings. Ask what each role can see and edit, and test it with the permissions you intend to grant.

Do not infer that a portal handles every change automatically. Verify cutoffs, payment adjustments and whether the booking history remains understandable after a reschedule.

## Calculate a realistic month
Estimate bookings multiplied by average service value for Cowlendar's revenue tier. For Appointo, choose the feature tier and add any relevant subscription/bundle or messaging costs. Use the same service mix in both calculations.

Then have the person responsible for the schedule run a test day in each system. A modest subscription difference can matter less than repeated manual corrections, but those corrections should be observed in your trial rather than assumed.

## Switch with a reconciliation plan
Export or document upcoming appointments, outstanding balances and repeat commitments. Confirm import support with the destination vendor. Keep the old system available until the future schedule and customer communications are reconciled.

# Cowlendar vs Sesami in 2026: Choosing a Shopify Booking Workflow

Compare Cowlendar and Sesami by resource model, retail customization, group bookings and the plan your Shopify business actually needs.

- Canonical: https://cowlendar.com/blog/cowlendar-vs-sesami-which-shopify-booking-app-is-better-in-2026
- Published: 2026-06-29T00:00:00.000Z
- Updated: 2026-09-22T16:38:32.222451Z
- Publisher: Cowlendar

## The short answer

Consider Sesami for a tailored retail booking experience and developer tooling. Consider Cowlendar for mixed booking types with a common feature set; compare the revenue tier you will need.

## Begin with the business you are building
The useful difference is not which app has the longest list. It is how your service operation should work. A retailer creating a custom consultation journey with an agency may value a different architecture from a merchant adding bookable activities to an existing store.

This guide explains the buying decision. Our [permanent Cowlendar vs Sesami comparison](/cowlendar-vs-sesami) contains the full feature table, current checked plans and source links. We publish Cowlendar, so treat our recommendation as a vendor's editorial perspective, not an independent test result.

## Understand the two pricing models
Cowlendar provides all features on the free plan, followed by booking-revenue tiers: $13.99 up to $1,000, $29.99 up to $3,000 and $59.99 up to $10,000.

Sesami's listing organizes paid plans by resources and capabilities. Small is $19 with five resources, Pro is $129 with twenty, and Premium is $299 with forty. The free option is for development stores. These monthly USD figures were checked September 22, 2026.

| Your requirement | What to examine |
| --- | --- |
| One-to-one retail appointments | Staff/resource assignment, POS workflow and customer changes |
| Group activities | Capacity behavior and the plan including groups |
| Several locations | Resource model, routing and the required tier |
| Custom storefront experience | Available APIs/SDK, implementation effort and maintenance |
| Rentals alongside appointments | Explicit date-range and shared inventory behavior |

## When Sesami deserves a close look
Sesami documents an API/SDK and POS support, which can matter when booking is part of a larger retail experience. Its higher tiers list groups, customer rescheduling, flows and multi-location capabilities.

If your agency plans a tailored interface, ask for a technical design before comparing subscriptions. Include development time, responsibility for theme updates and how errors are monitored. The ability to customize is valuable when there is a real requirement and a team to maintain it.

## When Cowlendar may be the simpler fit
Cowlendar explicitly lists one-to-one, group, multi-day, bundle and full-day bookings. A merchant combining several of those offers can evaluate them without first mapping each feature to a separate paid tier.

Usage allowances still apply to the free plan. Model the relevant revenue tier and ask support about any usage charges or requirements beyond the public plan description.

## Run a focused evaluation
Create the same service in both apps. Use the same duration, staff member, buffer, payment rule and customer information. Then attempt a conflicting reservation and a reschedule.

For a retail business, include the in-store staff workflow. For a group activity, test multiple attendees and a partial change. For a custom implementation, demonstrate both a successful booking and a failed request; customers need a usable recovery path.

## Plan a switch without losing appointments
Keep an inventory of future reservations and outstanding balances. Confirm the supported import method with the destination vendor. Run the new booking flow on an unpublished theme where possible, then reconcile availability before enabling it for customers.

Do not delete the old system until your team can account for future bookings, confirmations and payment obligations. The right choice is the system that fits your operation after launch, not only the more attractive demo.

## Official sources
- [Cowlendar Shopify listing](https://apps.shopify.com/cowlendar)
- [Sesami Shopify listing](https://apps.shopify.com/sesami)
- [Sesami developer documentation](https://sesami.dev/)


## Common questions

### Does Sesami have a free plan for live stores?

The checked free plan is for development stores. Live merchants should compare the paid tier that covers their resources and features.

### Does Cowlendar replace every custom Sesami implementation?

No. Evaluate APIs, resource rules and any custom storefront behavior individually. A standard booking widget and a bespoke implementation are different projects.

# Shopify Booking App Features: A Practical Buyer’s Checklist

Evaluate Shopify booking apps with a concrete checklist for availability, payments, reminders, staff, integrations and customer self-service.

- Canonical: https://cowlendar.com/blog/features-shopify-booking-app
- Published: 2025-07-06T00:00:00.000Z
- Updated: 2026-09-22T10:00:00Z
- Publisher: Cowlendar

## The short answer

Evaluate features as complete customer and staff workflows. A checkmark for “calendar sync” or “deposits” is only the beginning of the buying decision.

## Availability comes first
The booking engine must prevent the conflicts your business cannot accept. List the resources each service requires: a person, room, item, location or number of participant places. Check working hours, holidays, buffers and minimum notice.

Ask whether several required resources can be reserved together. An instructor and a room must both be free for the same session. For rentals, the system needs to protect the entire occupied date range, not just the pickup time.

## Check the meaning behind common features
| Feature label | What to verify |
| --- | --- |
| Calendar sync | Which calendars, which direction, which events block time, and expected delay |
| Group bookings | Capacity per session, participant counts and partial cancellations |
| Deposits | Amount collected now, remaining balance workflow and refund handling |
| Reminders | Channels, timing, supported languages and any usage charges |
| Multi-day bookings | End-date behavior, turnaround time and overlapping inventory |
| Staff management | Availability, access permissions, assignment and per-person costs |
| Booking packs | How a purchase creates credits and how visits consume them |
| Self-service | Cutoffs, rescheduling limits and updated confirmations |

## Follow the money through a change
Make a test payment, then cancel or move the booking. Verify the reservation status and Shopify order separately. If you use a deposit, check who collects the remaining amount and when. A feature named “partial payment” does not answer every operational question.

For subscriptions or bundles, include transaction-based charges in the comparison. For SMS, estimate message volume rather than comparing only the app subscription. Your true monthly budget includes the Shopify plan, relevant app tier and applicable usage costs.

## Inspect the customer experience on a phone
A booking widget should explain the selected service, date, time and time zone without forcing the customer to guess. Check text size, keyboard access, error messages and the transition into checkout. Test with a long service name and a narrow screen.

Look for clear loading and unavailable states. A calendar that appears empty should say why, or provide an alternative, rather than looking broken.

## Make staff access part of the evaluation
Ask the person who handles tomorrow's schedule to complete three tasks: find an appointment, move it, and explain its payment status. If they need access to the entire Shopify admin for a limited operational role, review whether that fits your permissions policy.

Confirm export options and the process for leaving the app. A good evaluation includes how future bookings, customer records and recurring commitments would be preserved during a switch.

## Score the requirements that matter
Divide requirements into essential, useful and optional. Reject an app that cannot enforce an essential availability rule even if its feature list is long. Among the remaining options, choose based on usability, total cost and support for your specific workflow.

Cowlendar documents appointments, groups, multi-day bookings, reminders, calendar connections and payment options. Our [features page](/features) explains the building blocks; the [comparison directory](/compare) shows documented differences across nine other apps.

## Official sources
- [Cowlendar features and pricing](https://apps.shopify.com/cowlendar)
- [Shopify service products](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/digital-service-product/selling-services-or-digital-products)


## Common questions

### What is the most important booking feature?

Accurate availability for the resources your service requires. Payments and a polished interface cannot compensate for a system that accepts conflicting reservations.

### Should I choose the app with the longest feature list?

No. First verify essential workflows, then compare usability and total cost. Some features are irrelevant to your business or only available on higher plans.

# Free Shopify Booking Apps in 2026: Limits, Pricing and Setup

Compare free Shopify appointment apps honestly: booking limits, service counts, staff restrictions and the features that require an upgrade.

- Canonical: https://cowlendar.com/blog/free-shopify-booking-apps-in-2026-reviews-pricing-and-setup
- Published: 2026-06-25T00:00:00.000Z
- Updated: 2026-09-22T16:38:32.222451Z
- Publisher: Cowlendar

## The short answer

“Free” can mean a small monthly allowance, unlimited bookings with restricted services, or development-store access only. Match the free plan to your complete workflow.

## What can you actually run for free?
Some free booking plans are suitable for an ongoing simple service. Others are best used to evaluate an app before upgrading. The important question is whether the free plan covers your booking volume and essential features together.

The following facts come from official listings checked September 22, 2026. This is a selection by Cowlendar, not an independent ranking. Shopify subscription and payment costs are separate from app pricing.

| App | Documented free allowance | Important boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cowlendar | Free plan; see usage allowance, all features | Paid tier needed beyond the allowance |
| Apntly | Unlimited bookings, 1 service, 1 staff member | Advanced features require paid plans |
| Appointo | Unlimited services and bookings | Reminders and calendar integrations are paid features |
| Easy Appointment Booking | 1 event, unlimited bookings/team | More advanced workflows require upgrades |
| Meety | Unlimited bookings and team members | Unlimited services and advanced capabilities vary by tier |
| BookThatApp | 10 bookings listed | Verify how that allowance is counted |
| Sesami | Development-store plan | Not a free live-store plan |

Hoppy also advertises a free plan, but the checked listing does not state a booking quota clearly enough for us to call it unlimited. Confirm the current limits with the vendor.

## Find the first feature that forces an upgrade
Calendar conflict detection, reminders, deposits and multiple staff are common decision points. A free plan with unlimited reservations may still require a paid tier for your working calendar connection.

Write down the essential features before comparing plans. For a solo free consultation, a narrow free plan may be enough. For paid group classes with waitlists and reminders, compare the appropriate paid plans from the start.

## Estimate the next stage, not only launch week
Model your expected service count, staff count, bookings and revenue. Check whether an upgrade is based on usage, resources or features. Include any messaging or subscription/bundle charges disclosed by the vendor.

Avoid configuring a business-critical workflow around a feature that disappears after a trial. Distinguish a permanent free tier from a temporary paid-plan trial in your notes.

## Set up and test one real service
1. Create a representative service product with a clear duration and price.
2. Configure availability, staff, buffers and booking notice.
3. Add the supported booking widget to the correct product template.
4. Complete a booking on a phone using a customer email address.
5. Test a conflict, cancellation and any payment change.
6. Confirm which plan features were active during the test.

Cowlendar's free plan lets you evaluate all features before choosing a paid revenue tier. If you need unlimited ongoing free bookings for a simple service, compare the other documented options fairly. The best free choice is the one that stays usable for your actual operation.

# Google Calendar Appointment Schedules vs Cowlendar

Choose between Google Calendar appointment schedules and Cowlendar for Shopify, based on checkout, service products, groups and calendar needs.

- Canonical: https://cowlendar.com/blog/google-calendar-appointments-versus-cowlendar
- Published: 2024-06-03T00:00:00.000Z
- Updated: 2026-09-22T16:38:32.222451Z
- Publisher: Cowlendar

## The short answer

Google Calendar appointment schedules suit a calendar-first booking page. Cowlendar is designed around bookable Shopify products, store checkout and several service formats.

## Compare the job each tool is doing
Google Calendar appointment schedules let people choose available times through a booking page. Cowlendar turns Shopify products into bookable services. Both can help a customer reserve time, but they start from different business systems.

If you only need someone to choose a consultation slot, begin with the simplest tool that meets that need. If the booking should be part of your Shopify catalog and order workflow, evaluate the storefront integration carefully.

## Understand Google's free and paid boundaries
Google documents a single booking page for a personal Google account. Additional capabilities depend on an eligible Google Workspace or Google One subscription, and the eligibility is not identical for every premium feature.

Payment collection through Stripe is available with eligible Workspace subscriptions. Do not assume that any paid Google plan includes paid appointments, multiple calendars and automated reminders. Check Google's current feature table against the exact account you use.

| Requirement | Google Calendar approach | Shopify booking app approach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Share an available time | Dedicated booking page | Bookable service in the storefront |
| Sell alongside products | Requires evaluating a separate commerce flow | Designed around Shopify products and orders |
| Collect payment | Stripe on eligible Workspace plans | Supported booking/payment flow through the store setup |
| Group or multi-day services | Verify the specific schedule model | Select an app that explicitly supports the format |
| Staff and shared resources | Depends on calendar/account setup | Depends on the app's resource rules and plan |

## When Google Calendar is a sensible choice
A consultant who already works in Google Calendar and needs a simple appointment page may not need a Shopify booking app at all. Test conflict detection, booking questions, reminders and the customer-facing confirmation with the relevant account.

If the booking is free or does not belong in your store's order history, a separate booking page may be perfectly adequate. Consider the cost of the eligible Google subscription only when you need its paid capabilities.

## When Cowlendar fits better
Cowlendar is worth evaluating when customers should discover a service in your Shopify store, select a date or time and follow the configured store payment flow. It lists groups, multi-day bookings, bundles, deposits and several calendar/meeting integrations.

Its free plan includes all features; paid plans follow booking-revenue tiers. That is a different cost model from a Google subscription. Compare the total system you need, including Shopify, rather than claiming that either option is universally cheaper.

## Test calendar conflicts rather than assuming sync
Create a busy event in the relevant external calendar, then check whether the customer can still choose that time. Test a cancellation and a reschedule in both directions supported by the tool. Record where staff should make changes.

Also test a customer in another time zone. The displayed local time, confirmation and staff event must represent the same instant. Our [timezone converter](/free-tools/timezone-converter) helps compare locations when planning the test.

## Official sources
- [Google: create an appointment schedule](https://support.google.com/calendar/answer/11608416?hl=en)
- [Google: premium appointment schedule features](https://support.google.com/calendar/answer/16287038?hl=en)
- [Google: paid appointments](https://support.google.com/calendar/answer/13762729?hl=en)
- [Cowlendar Shopify listing](https://apps.shopify.com/cowlendar)


## Common questions

### Can Google Calendar take payment for an appointment?

Yes, through Stripe with eligible Google Workspace subscriptions. Check the exact account eligibility; not every Google plan includes the same premium features.

### Can I use Google Calendar with Cowlendar?

Cowlendar lists Google Calendar integration. Configure the connection and test which events block availability and how booking changes synchronize.

# How to Sell and Book Workshop Events on Shopify

Build a workshop booking flow on Shopify with session dates, participant capacity, clear tickets and a practical check-in process.

- Canonical: https://cowlendar.com/blog/how-to-book-workshop-events-using-shopify-apps
- Published: 2025-07-24T00:00:00.000Z
- Updated: 2026-09-22T10:00:00Z
- Publisher: Cowlendar

## The short answer

Sell a place in a specific session, not just a generic workshop product. The booking must connect the date, number of attendees, payment and remaining capacity.

## Define what one purchase reserves
Start with a workshop people can understand in one glance: what they will make or learn, where it happens, how long it lasts and what is included. Clarify whether the displayed price is per person, per group or for a private session.

A customer buying quantity three should reserve three participant places if that is your intended model. Test this explicitly. Some configurations treat product quantity, attendee count and number of bookings as separate values.

## Build the session schedule
Create the workshop product, then connect the booking app and configure the permitted dates. Assign the instructor and room if their availability is limited. Add setup and cleanup time around each session so the next group does not arrive while the previous group is still finishing.

For recurring workshops, verify that editing one date does not unexpectedly change every future session. Holidays, guest instructors and special editions are easier to manage when the distinction between a recurring rule and an individual session is clear.

## Choose the right capacity model
| Offer | Capacity should represent | Useful intake |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public pottery class | Participant seats | Names and relevant accessibility needs |
| Private team workshop | One group or one session | Group size and organizer details |
| Parent-and-child activity | The actual resources used | Adult/child count, where required |
| Workshop series | Each session in the series | Attendance and scheduling expectations |

Do not use a single product stock number as a substitute for date-specific capacity unless your setup explicitly maintains that relationship.

## Make the confirmation operational
Include the selected date, start time and time zone, venue directions, arrival time and contact details. Tell customers what to bring and what happens if they arrive late. Explain how attendee names can be changed without accidentally canceling the order.

If you use booking questions for dietary or accessibility requirements, collect only what is needed and restrict staff access appropriately. Avoid sending sensitive intake answers to every participant in a group email.

## Run a sold-out and cancellation test
Purchase the last two places, then attempt another booking. Cancel one place according to your policy and check whether exactly one seat returns. If there is a waitlist, verify whether joining it reserves anything and how a person is invited to pay when a space opens.

Cowlendar supports group bookings and participant workflows. Easy Appointment Booking lists packs and waitlists on its higher plans; Meety also separates these features by tier. Compare the cost of the complete workflow, including staff access and reminders, before choosing.

## Give the instructor a usable attendance list
Before launch, simulate the day of the workshop. The instructor should be able to identify the session, see the expected attendees and distinguish paid, canceled and changed bookings. Reconcile the list with the booking system after any last-minute edit.

For online sessions, continue with our [workshop and webinar ticket guide](/blog/how-to-sell-workshop-and-webinar-tickets-on-your-shopify-store), which covers meeting links and access instructions.

## Official sources
- [Cowlendar group booking](https://apps.shopify.com/cowlendar)
- [Easy Appointment Booking plans](https://apps.shopify.com/appointments-and-bookings)
- [Meety event features](https://apps.shopify.com/meety-appointment-booking)


## Common questions

### Can customers buy several workshop seats at once?

Many booking apps support group or participant bookings, but verify how participant count relates to Shopify product quantity and session capacity.

### Does a waitlist guarantee a place?

Usually it expresses interest rather than a confirmed reservation. Explain your actual notification, payment and expiry process to customers.
